summary: A link-in-bio page on your own domain: your links live in one JSON file, every button routes through a redirect that counts the click without a third party, and a private stats page shows what people actually press. Fast, dark-mode aware, and yours.

stack.why: the page is server-rendered HTML and the redirect is one INSERT and a 302
editing a file and redeploying is the CMS; git is the history
content is a file; only the counters need a database
the redirect needs a process; the rest is static

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your links, title and bio, written down
prerequisites.why: The page renders links.json exactly. Decide the order and titles first so Phase 1 is about rendering, not editing.
prerequisites.get: A list of up to ten links with a short title each, a one-line bio, and a square avatar image (at least 400x400).

prerequisites.name: A random salt for hashing IPs
prerequisites.why: Click rows store a daily-salted hash, never the raw address.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: The entire upgrade over Linktree is that the page lives on your domain.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base URL for OG tags.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: The page
phases.goal: Render the profile and links from links.json, mobile-first, working with JavaScript disabled, and refuse to boot on a broken file.

steps.detail: profile (name, bio, avatar, accent) and links: array of {slug, title, url, emoji, enabled}. The slug is the permanent click-tracking key; changing a title must never change a slug.
commands: mkdir links && cd links && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.detail: Every url starts with http, every slug is unique and lowercase, avatar exists in public/. On failure exit with the bad entry named. A broken page is worse than a refused start.
Avatar, name, bio, then enabled links as a vertical stack of buttons. Disabled links do not render at all.

check: The page renders at 375px with JavaScript disabled and every link navigates
A malformed links.json stops the server with a message naming the bad entry
A link with enabled false is absent from the HTML

phases.title: Design

steps.do: Set the typographic hierarchy and 44px tap targets
steps.detail: System font stack; buttons at least 44px tall with generous horizontal padding.

steps.do: Read the accent into a CSS custom property and add dark mode
steps.detail: prefers-color-scheme with the same custom properties overridden. Check contrast in both schemes.

steps.do: Add hover, active and focus-visible states
steps.detail: Keyboard visitors must see where they are.

check: Zero third-party network requests on load
No contrast failures in either color scheme in an accessibility audit
Every button is reachable and operable by keyboard
traps: No web fonts from a CDN. A fonts request is a third-party call and a performance deduction.

phases.title: Click tracking
phases.goal: Every button goes through /go/:slug, which records a row and redirects, and the redirect never waits on the database.

steps.detail: clicks (id, slug, clicked_at, referer_host, user_agent_class, ip_hash). Classify the user agent into mobile, desktop or bot at write time and store the bucket, not the string.
Look up the slug in links.json, send the 302 first, then insert the row. Unknown slugs redirect to / rather than erroring.

steps.do: Hash the IP with a daily salt
steps.detail: sha256(IP_SALT + today's date + ip). The same visitor is one hash today and a different one tomorrow.

steps.do: Add rel="noopener noreferrer" to outbound links

check: Clicking a link lands on the target and adds one row
An unknown slug lands on the homepage
Stopping SQLite mid-test still redirects correctly and drops the row
traps: Send the redirect before writing. A click must never wait on the database.

phases.title: Bot filtering and stats
phases.goal: A private stats page whose numbers you can explain.

steps.do: Bucket bot user agents at write time
steps.detail: A short list (bot, crawler, spider, preview, slackbot, twitterbot, facebookexternalhit). Count them separately rather than deleting them.
Clicks per link over today, 7 and 30 days excluding bots, a clicks-per-day bar chart as inline SVG, top referrers, and the bot count shown separately.

check: Totals reconcile with a GROUP BY slug query
A curl with a bot user agent is bucketed as bot and excluded from the headline number
The page renders with zero clicks recorded

phases.title: Share cards and deploy
phases.goal: Previews correctly when shared, live on your domain, documented.

steps.do: Add OG and Twitter meta plus a generated 1200x630 OG image
steps.detail: satori and @resvg/resvg-js at startup or build time, rendering your name on your accent.

steps.do: Add /healthz, a nightly backup command, and the systemd unit
Point the domain, deploy, write the README
steps.detail: README: the links.json reference, the warning that slugs are permanent, how to add a link without breaking stats, and a note that owning the domain is the actual upgrade.

check: The link previews correctly in a card validator
A reader goes from clone to a live page on their own domain using only the README

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product-builder path: know when the redirect is down, never lose the database, and keep the server patched.

steps.do: Add a /healthz endpoint and an external uptime check against it
steps.detail: Answer 200 with the build id and a quick database read. Point a free uptime monitor (or your own, from the Healthchecks entry on this site) at it so an outage is noticed before a user notices.

steps.do: Write structured request logs and rotate them
steps.detail: One JSON line per request: method, path, status, duration, no raw IPs. Rotate weekly with logrotate, keep eight.

steps.do: Back the SQLite file up off the machine nightly and test a restore
steps.detail: SQLite's .backup command makes a consistent copy while the app runs. Copy it to object storage or a second machine; then, once, restore it into a fresh checkout and confirm the app reads it.
Firewall allowing only 22, 80 and 443; unattended security updates on; the app running as an unprivileged user under systemd with Restart=on-failure.

check: Stopping the service triggers an uptime alert within a few minutes
A restore from last night's backup contains yesterday's data
A port scan from another machine shows only 22, 80 and 443

product.outcome: A link page you could run for a small roster of people or brands: content as files, click data you own, a domain that never changes hands.

architecture.swap: Any source yielding the same object; a small admin UI could write the file

architecture.owns: the server-rendered page and OG image
architecture.swap: Could be a static build; the /go routes are the only dynamic part
A serverless function writing the same rows
Any UI over the clicks table

operations.backup: links.json is in git. SQLite .backup nightly for clicks, thirty days kept.
operations.restore: Deploy from git; copy the clicks backup into place. Nothing else exists.
operations.monitoring: Uptime check on /healthz. A sudden zero in clicks per day during normal traffic means the redirect is broken.
operations.incident: A hijacked link in links.json is fixed by a commit and redeploy; the history shows when it changed.

releaseGate: A clean clone reaches a live page using only the README
Bot traffic verified excluded from headline numbers with a seeded fixture
One restore drill performed and dated

notIncluded: The drag-and-drop editor. Editing links.json is the trade for owning it.
Their analytics beyond clicks per link. At this scale the only question is which link people press.
Payments, link scheduling, and the integrations you were not using.
after: A tiny basic-auth editor that writes links.json and commits it
